item.title: Combining Manual Retouching and Inpainting
item.description:
Even with SDXL or LoRA, characters with complex designs—such as different hair colors on each side—often suffer from color bleeding. Controlling these details perfectly with prompts alone is difficult. This guide introduces a highly reliable correction method that combines "base painting" in image editing software with "Inpainting."Tools Used: Inpainting: ComfyUI Image Editing: CLIP STUDIO PAINT When generating characters with complex color schemes, colors often bleed into each other or merge into a single tone, even when using a LoRA. Furthermore, if there is a significant contrast between the original color and the target color, the Inpainting function may fail to override the existing pixels, resulting in artifacts or incorrect color reflection.To improve Inpainting accuracy, we manually place "guide colors" using image editing software beforehand. Coloring with the Bucket Tool: Directly apply the desired color to the area you want to change (e.g., the left side of the hair) using a bucket or fill tool. Color Selection Tip: Use the eyedropper tool to pick colors from existing parts of the image. This helps the new color blend naturally with the overall lighting and tone. Acceptance of Roughness: At this stage, a flat "bucket fill" is perfectly fine. As long as the basic shape is defined, the AI will interpret it as a structure. [Original Image] The character is designed to have "blue hair on the left and red on the right," but the initial generation resulted in a uniform color. Replicating such specific details has a low success rate with prompts or LoRA alone, necessitating a final touch-up via Inpainting.
[Retouching (Base Painting)] Use the bucket tool in your editing software to place the color directly onto the target area. In this example, the left side of the hair was changed to cyan.
[After Inpainting] Run the retouched image through Inpainting to blend it with the surroundings. The previously flat-colored area now has realistic hair texture and highlights.When loading the color-adjusted image into Stable Diffusion's Inpainting, ensure the character LoRA is active. Leveraging LoRA: If the character LoRA is enabled, the AI will automatically correct the area to the "intended hue and texture" based on the LoRA's training data, even without detailed color prompts. The Benefit: By combining your manual "color guide" with the LoRA's "textural information," you achieve a seamless finish in the shortest amount of time. To realize your prompt's intent, retouching the image into a similar form before applying Inpainting will drastically increase the success rate.
